title: Configuring Notification Templates for Zscaler Client Connector

blocks.text: You can configure notification templates to control which notifications display for end users in Zscaler Client Connector. You assign a notification template to an app profile and Zscaler Client Connector displays notifications based on the platform and the version of Zscaler Client Connector.
There are two types of notification templates:

blocks.item: Modern: Provides options to control which individual notifications or groups of notifications display and for how long for each selected platform. End users can’t manually change which notifications display from the app and can only temporarily pause them using Do not Disturb. Available for Zscaler Client Connector versions 5.0 and later. Contact Zscaler Support to enable this feature.

Legacy: Provides options to control which notification types display (but not how the individual notifications display). End users can manually enable or disable some notifications. Available for Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0.

blocks.text: Zscaler made notification templates generally available in May 2026. Existing global settings to enable default, app update, Internet & SaaS (ZIA), and Private Access (ZPA) reauthentication notifications as well as persistence settings from the End User Notifications tab were migrated to a Legacy Notification Settings template that applies to all users by default until they are assigned a template in the app profile. For Zscaler Client Connector versions 4.8 to 4.10 for Windows, you can create additional templates and assign them to Windows app profiles.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > End User Notification > Client Connector.
On the Templates tab, click Add Template.
See image.

If the Modern template feature isn't enabled on your tenant, the tab is called the Notification Template tab, and you can click the Add button to configure a template that includes only legacy settings.
On the Add Template page, configure the following under Common Settings:
Name: Enter a name for the template. You cannot change the default Legacy Notification Settings template name.

Popup Duration (Seconds): Enter the value from 5 to 60 to set the number of seconds that Zscaler Client Connector pop-up notifications display. The default value is 5. Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector for Windows and macOS.

Do not Disturb: Enable to include a Do not Disturb button on Zscaler Client Connector pop-up notifications. The default value is disabled. Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector for Windows and macOS and the Zscaler notification framework must be enabled.
See image.

If the Modern template feature isn't enabled on your tenant, the Common Settings section doesn't display. You can set the pop-up duration in the Custom Timer (In Seconds) field and enable the Do not disturb setting in the legacy settings.
Under Notification Settings, select the tab for the type of template to configure:
Modern

The settings on this tab apply to users with this template assigned in the app profile who also use Zscaler Client Connector versions 5.0 and later. For users with Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0, the Legacy tab settings apply.
On the Modern tab:
Platforms: Select one or more platforms to configure notifications for.
Notification Categories: Select the categories of notifications you want to configure. If you don’t select a category, no notifications for that category will display.
For each selected platform, enable or disable each selected category. Some categories aren’t available for all platforms and display as Not Available for that platform.
If you enabled a category and want to configure how individual notifications within the category display:

Under Category-Wide Settings, enable or disable the Persistent option to indicate whether to display the notifications for that category until the user dismisses them. Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

If this setting is enabled, you can still disable the Persistent option per individual notification (e.g., you can enable the Persistent option for the category and disable the Persistent option for one of the notifications). If this setting is disabled, you can’t enable the option for individual notifications.
Under Notification Messages, for each notification you can configure these options:
Notification: Enable this option to display the notification. If disabled, the notification never displays.
Persistent: If available, enable this option to display the notification until the user dismisses it. If disabled, the notification displays until the Popup Duration (Seconds) is reached.
See image.
Legacy

The settings on this tab apply to users with this template assigned in the app profile who also use Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0. For users with Zscaler Client Connector versions 5.0 and later, the settings on the Modern tab apply.
Some notifications are available only for Zscaler Client Connector for Windows and macOS and require the Zscaler Notification Framework. To learn more, see Using the Zscaler Notification Framework.
On the Legacy tab:

Show Zscaler Client Connector Notification Popups by Default: Select this option to have users receive pop-up notifications from Zscaler Client Connector. This setting is enabled after a user is enrolled. Users can turn this option off from Zscaler Client Connector in the More window in the app.
Enable App Updates Notifications: Select this option to have users receive app upgrade notifications.
Enable Service Status Notifications: Select this option to have users receive status notifications for Zscaler services, such as when a service is in Disaster Relief (DR) mode.

For Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0 for macOS, you must also enable the system-based notification settings to display service status notifications, even if the Zscaler Notification Framework is enabled.

Enable ZIA Notifications: Select this option to have users receive notifications from Internet & SaaS (ZIA), such as data loss prevention (DLP) notifications. To learn more, see About Zscaler Client Connector-Based End User Notifications.

Enable Notifications for ZPA reauthentication: Select this option to have users prompted for authentication. This option is enabled after a user is enrolled. Users can turn this option off from Zscaler Client Connector in the More window in the app.

For Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0 for macOS, you must also enable the system-based notification settings to display service status notifications, even if the Zscaler Notification Framework is enabled.

Show ZPA Reauthentication Notifications Every (In Minutes): Select this option to show Private Access (ZPA) reauthentication notifications at a specific time interval. This setting is enabled by default. Enter a value from 2 to 1440 to set the interval in minutes.

Enable Persistent Notifications: When enabled, overrides the Custom Timer. This setting displays critical notifications until the user dismisses them. Critical notifications include Private Access reauthentication, captive portal detection, and request for a system reboot.
ZIA Notification Persistent: When enabled, overrides the Custom Timer and makes Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) notifications persistent.

Delay Posture Failure Notifications after Tunnel Establishment (In Seconds): When enabled, Zscaler Client Connector delays pop-up notifications for device posture failure for the number of entered seconds after a system reboot. The default value is 0. You can enter a value up to 300.

This option helps prevent user confusion and unnecessary resolution attempts. For example, after a device restart, Zscaler Client Connector evaluates the Detect CrowdStrike device posture but because CrowdStrike is still starting, the device posture check fails temporarily and Private Access blocks access based on the access policy. You can use this option to delay the notification and allow time for the device posture to pass.

This option delays only the pop-up notification (not the message that displays in the Notifications window in the app). Zscaler Client Connector automatically suppresses duplicate messages that display within a two-minute interval, so subsequent posture failure notifications won’t display for an additional 120 seconds.

For example, if this option is set to 60 seconds and a posture failure notification is received within 15 seconds of a reboot, the pop-up notification is suppressed. If an additional failure notification is received 90 seconds after reboot, the pop-up notification is still suppressed because it is within two minutes of the first notification.

ZIA Firewall: Select this option to show firewall notifications from Internet & SaaS in the Notifications window in the app. If enabled, you can select Firewall Popup Notifications to also display them as pop-up notifications. To learn more, see Configuring EUNs for Firewall Filtering.

DNS: Select this option to show DNS notifications from Internet & SaaS in the Notifications window in the app. If enabled, you can select DNS Popup Notifications to also display them as pop-up notifications. To learn more, see Configuring EUNs for DNS Control.

IPS: Select this option to show IPS notifications from Internet & SaaS in the Notifications window in the app. If enabled, you can select IPS Popup Notifications to also display them as pop-up notifications. To learn more, see Configuring EUNs for IPS Control.
You must also select Enable ZIA Notifications to display the ZIA Firewall, DNS, and IPS notifications for users.

Show Device Posture Failure Remediation Notification: Select this option to show a pop-up notification if a Private Access app is blocked because a device posture that is included in an access policy fails and Device Posture Failure Notification is enabled on the access policy.

If this option is enabled, the pop-up notification from Private Access displays and includes a Learn More link that, when clicked, opens the Zscaler Client Connector app and displays the Message from the Device Posture Profile in the Notifications window.
See image.
Click Save.

blocks.text: After you create a template, you can assign it to the Notification Template in the app profile to apply the notification settings to a group of users. Users with Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later receive notifications based on the Modern tab configuration. Users with Zscaler Client Connector versions earlier than 5.0 receive notifications based on the Legacy tab configuration.
